title: The hidden costs of being public: Evidence from multinational firms operating in an emerging market

rival_explanations: size (larger firms get more regulatory attention, not listing status)
global trends / factors other than differential compliance costs driving the M&A patterns
domicile of the acquirer (domestic vs foreign firm) driving the results

context.time_period: 2000-2015 overall (import/customs transactions January 2010-September 2014; M&A transactions 2000-2015, extended to 2017 for the aftermath test)
context.sample_description: Two main samples. (1) Import transactions from a novel Argentine customs database (matched to exporters via WIPO Global Brand Database) for Harmonized System codes 84.07, 84.08, 84.09, imported by MNC affiliates and independent domestic distributors; observations restricted to importers with complete importer/brand/model info and at least 1000 units imported over 2010-2014, dropping ARS-denominated transactions. (2) M&A transactions from Bureau Van Dijk's Zephyr database where an MNC's Argentine subsidiary was sold, excluding regulated industries (utilities SIC 4900-4949 and financial institutions SIC 6000-6999).
context.sample_size: ~850,000 import transactions and 73 importers (20 listed MNCs and 13 private MNCs) for the compliance analysis; 1,492 M&A transactions (subsample of 762 with acquirer stake >=95%) for the M&A analysis

data_sources.name: Manual internet search coding of firm relatedness and parent-company ownership (listed vs. private)
Central Bank of Argentina (repatriation of earnings and royalties by industry; added value)
